transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess I’m here because... honestly, things have just been really off ever since my father-in-law moved in with us. He used to have this great little place over in Elmwood, you know, one of those nice brick ranchers with the big oak trees in the front yard? Beautiful property, really, but the property taxes there just went through the roof last year. It's ridiculous what they're charging for county services now, especially for seniors on a fixed income. 

But anyway, since he moved into our spare room, I’ve just been... I don't know, I keep snapping at my wife over every little house thing. And I've been putting off all these jobs and paperwork that I used to stay right on top of. The mail just piles up on the kitchen island now. Speaking of the mail, we got a new carrier last month and he keeps leaving the box open, so half the envelopes get soaked if it rains. I keep meaning to call the post office about it, but I just haven't. 

I just can’t seem to get my head quiet lately. Even when I try to get away and go out to my workshop, or when I'm trying to fish. I actually went out to the lake on Tuesday to try out this new crankbait I bought—it's this chartreuse color, supposed to be absolutely killer for bass when the water's a bit murky—but I didn't even care about casting once I got out there. I just sat in the boat. My brain just kept spinning and I couldn't shut it off.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much enjoyment out of things you usually like, like fishing or working in your workshop?

I mean, I'm not really sure if it's that I don't enjoy them anymore. I haven't really noticed a lack of enjoyment, exactly. Like with the workshop... I love that space. I actually spent three weeks last summer building this custom workbench out of reclaimed barn wood. You should see the grain on this wood, it's absolutely gorgeous. I got it from this guy over in Miller's Creek who was tearing down his grandfather's old dairy farm. 

It's kind of sad, really, seeing all these old family farms getting bought up by corporate developers. They're putting in another one of those massive subdivisions out there, you know the ones with the identical vinyl-siding houses stacked right on top of each other? Traffic on Route 9 is going to be an absolute nightmare once all those people move in. They haven't even widened the intersection by the gas station yet. 

But, uh... yeah, I don't know if I've lost the enjoyment for my hobbies. I just haven't really thought about it like that.
Over the past few weeks, have you found yourself losing interest in activities you usually enjoy, like fishing or working in your workshop?

Well, like I was just saying... I haven't really noticed losing interest, no. It's not that I don't care about the workshop or the fishing. I mean, I was just looking at the fishing gear catalogs the other day. They've got these new sonar fish finders that are just incredible. You hook them up right to your smartphone, and the resolution is so clear you can practically see the fins on the fish. Technology is just wild these days, isn't it? My nephew, he's 19, he was showing me how he can control the thermostat in his apartment from his phone while he's sitting in class. Which, honestly, seems a bit much. When I was his age, if you were cold, you just put on a sweater. 

But yeah, I haven't really felt like I'm losing interest in things. I just haven't been doing them as much, I guess.
Have you been feeling down or sad most of the day, more days than not, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Well, no, not really down or sad, I don't think. I mean, I'm not sitting around crying or anything. It's more just... I don't know, my head's just loud, like I said. But sad? No. Although, you know what is sad? They just announced they're closing down that old hardware store on Main Street. The one with the creaky wooden floors? Hank's Hardware. Been there since, gosh, the fifties, I think. Hank's grandson has been running it, but I guess he can't compete with those big box stores out on the highway. 

It's a real shame. You used to be able to go in there and actually buy just three screws if that's all you needed, instead of having to buy a plastic blister pack of fifty that you can't even open without a pair of heavy-duty shears. I swear, the packaging they use nowadays is practically bulletproof. I cut my thumb wide open last month trying to get a new flashlight out of one of those packages. Bled like a stuck pig. My wife had to get the special bandages out of the first aid kit. 

But, uh, no, to answer your question, I haven't really been feeling sad or down most of the day. Just... off.

The focus on stress related to life changes (father-in-law moving in, work/home stressors) with associated difficulty coping suggests an adjustment disorder.
